entities.name: All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), founded in 1972 by M. G. Ramachandran (MGR) — one of Tamil cinema's greatest stars who turned mass film popularity into political power — is one of India's two dominant regional parties in Tamil Nadu, the state that is home to India's most politically self-conscious regional identity, the Dravidian movement. AIADMK has ruled Tamil Nadu for extended periods and has influenced national politics through coalition arrangements.

M. G. Ramachandran broke from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) in 1972 after clashing with DMK leader M. Karunanidhi. MGR's film stardom — he had played heroic roles embodying working-class virtue for 30 years — translated directly into electoral support; his personal popularity was so immense that his death (1987) triggered mass grief unprecedented in modern Indian politics, with hundreds of reported suicides among devotees. Under MGR, AIADMK became one of India's most powerful regional parties.

Afterhim, the party was led by Jayalalithaa (J. Jayalalithaa, 1987-2016), another iconic Tamil film actress turned politician, who served as Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister six times. Jayalalithaa's tenure was marked by both populist welfare schemes (noon meal programs, free goods distribution) and corruption controversies (the Tansi land deal, disproportionate assets case). The AIADMK's Dravidian identity — rooted in anti-Brahmin rationalist social reform movements — distinguishes it from Hindi-belt national parties and reflects Tamil Nadu's unique political culture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: AIADMK — founded by a film star whose death triggered mass grief, led by Jayalalithaa for three decades of welfare populism, and representing Tamil Nadu's distinctive Dravidian political culture — is one of India's most culturally unique and electorally significant regional parties.
